This is the number one feature request of the in-engine script editor, so I look forward to give it a spin!

This is perhaps a stupid question, but I’m asking it anyway; what are the limitations of this simpler method? Or in other words, what cases can this simpler method never address that the more complex implementation by @adamscott’s PR can?

> what are the limitations of this simpler method?

Potentially, the alternative could detect symbol usages in more complex contexts. Like `object["property"]`, `object.get("property")`, `object.call("method")`, etc. But I think this approach is quite good and significantly simpler (see [Pareto principle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pareto_principle)).

Essentially, this is assisted renaming, which is entirely justified for dynamic and gradually typed languages ​​like GDScript. Our main goal is to eliminate false-positive detection of symbol usages (checkboxes should be automatically selected only for safe occurrences). False-negative detection is less of a problem; the user can manually check occurrences that the editor cannot confidently classify (due to dynamic context or implicit access).

First of all: This is approach is totally valid, it's what the language server has been doing for years.

IMO this should not live in editor code. We need to stop treating `lookup_code` as a "one solution fits all" method in the public API. There is behaviour which makes sense for hover hints (e.g. resolving identifiers in comments), but for renaming you generally don't want that. (I'm not saying that the implementation needs to be changed to introduce this feature, I'm just talking about how to structure the API.)

A few takeaways from the language server that might be relevant to this PR:
- `lookup_code` is not exactly fast. An optimization like https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/115851 should be in place to prevent calling it if possible. (Another reason why this should not be implemented in general editor code, because this optimization requires knowledge about the languages syntax)
- The LSP applies additional resolve logic to fix `lookup_code` on declarations. This should mostly be not necessary anymore with https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/102937 however enum items are still not resolved by `lookup_code` iirc
- `lookup_code` isn't exactly good in terms of correctness and a lot of this will probably never be fixed since some people consider it useful for hover hints. -> at least in the public API we should split this from the API for hover hints.
Another limitation is that `lookup_code()` and the find/rename function only work on saved files. It won't find unsaved changes.

Is it also acceptable that this simpler solution can be implemented as a stopgap in case users do want more than assisted renaming?

> Another limitation is that `lookup_code()` and the find/rename function only work on saved files. It won't find unsaved changes.

this is a pretty big caveat… hmm…

To my knowledge, `lookup_code` does respect the unsaved changes for the current file in which it is called (based on the passed source code). When it comes to other unsaved files, it will use the state from disk.
Well, the lookup is always done on the "current" script (i.e. script where the result was found), so it should be fine? It does work, from my testing.

Then we have a safety buffer until we add a patch that actually fixes the scene files. > Before we double down on this workaround, do 'we' see a path towards actually fixing the scene files too? Because it will almost certainly be the most requested feature after this 'simple symbol renaming' method is implemented. I do have a major gripe with this popup, which is that it doesn't specify how one can rename exported properties 'manually' without having to re-reference all the objects / re-enter all the values in the inspector. And that in particular is complicated and messy - see the discussion on https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/10644 - requiring tool scripts if it needs to be automated. Perhaps the 'manually' needs to be spelled out more, or the functionality to preserve / rename properties should be implemented alongside this PR?

> Before we double down on this workaround, do 'we' see a path towards actually fixing the scene files too?

It's possible to search .tscn files and find matching properties, but there is no easy way to identify that these are the renamed properties or just something that shares their name. Though maybe that's not a problem?

Also not sure if it's possible with binary scenes.

> but there is no easy way to identify that these are the renamed properties or just something that shares their name.

Am I missing something here? Aren't objects always serialized together with their script? Couldn't we just skip all objects with a script that does not match?

> Couldn't we just skip all objects with a script that does not match?

FindInFiles does not load the scene, it searches it as plain text. So the script needs to be identified somehow. It requires either:
- Doing some basic manual parsing of the scene.
- Loading the scene and finding the node with the matching property.

Both aren't exactly trivial.

> Another limitation is that `lookup_code()` and the find/rename function only work on saved files. It won't find unsaved changes.

Just warn the user of the limitation. If there are unsaved files, advise the user that unsaved files won't get refactored and prompt them if they want unsaved files to be saved before applying the patch.

But it's a lot of work, I get that. Perhaps we can work towards a first version that uses the Find in Files dock (😢) and then have a followup PR for an improved Rename dock. Regardless, in the next few weeks I won't have time to create another design that could be based more on the Find in Files panel because I'm prepping for gamescom... I'll ask other usability team members to take a look.

To what extent would it be feasible / would you be willing to modify the Find in Files when in rename symbol mode? I can imagine the following changes, which only enable and disable specific things depending on whether you are in rename symbol mode: - hide the entire header of the right panel. we don't need any of that info & functionality while we're renaming a symbol. - add the (read only) rename symbol field to the left panel which has the symbol name we're renaming. - labels and buttons could use slightly different texts so that it's a bit clearer what you're doing in the panel. the result: Is that more feasible? EDIT: - maybe the panel needs one more ugly button somewhere (temporarily) to 'exit' rename symbol mode and return to the find in files state of the panel. or maybe I'm missing how else people could exit rename symbol mode?

Note that Apply/Discard buttons are inspired by VS Code I did not implement Discard in the end, because even that was annoying to add :P The current way to exit the mode is either apply changes, or close the tab when you have multiple search tabs open. Hiding the whole header would make switching the tabs not possible. Not sure what should happen when you start a new search without exiting rename mode; currently it just opens a new tab.

The apply / discard texts on the button work there because they're underneath the list with the checkboxes. The last version of your PR put 'Apply' underneath the input field which can also imply that the text you entered is applied to the preview, not necessarily renaming everything. But now we're veering deep into UX land; let's stay out of that.

I think it's important to the usability of this feature to have the name of the symbol that you're renaming side by side with the text you want it replaced with, so if you want to keep the header with the tabs, then maybe you can hide the "find:    [symbol]" label in the header so that the field (like in my last preview) has it?

Per discussion on chat, I marked the renaming as experimental, to better convey its current state: This dialog appears every time you confirm renaming: (it's not going to stay permanently)

At the risk of bikeshedding (and/or bikeshedding-adjacent behavior), there are two minor notes I have on the popup:

- Is it standard in Godot to have the "confirm" item on the left, and the "cancel" on the right? In other software I use, I think it's more typical to do the opposite. Since English is read left-to-right, the right-hand button makes sense to be the "move foward" button.
  - On the other hand, reversing the order here could be good. If someone is going through this on autopilot and they click the right-hand button to move forward without reading or understanding the potential consequences of their actions, in this case they'll instead cancel the operation.
- The "confirm" button saying "I understand the risk" maybe could say something like "I understand the risk, continue" so that it's more explicitly performing the operation? Or there could be a checkbox above for "I understand the risk", which enables the "Continue" button when checked... but that might be a lot of extra work for not much benefit 😅
Meorge, I love the attitude and your insights are valid, so don't take it personally that I'm about to completely ignore it and merge this anyway
Haha, no worries. It's gonna be an awesome feature for 4.8! And I suppose there's still time during the beta period to tweak wording on stuff, if it's deemed necessary at all 😄
Thanks!

> Is it standard in Godot to have the "confirm" item on the left, and the "cancel" on the right?

That's a standard ConfirmationDialog, so it's not specific to this popup. The order is defined by `accept_dialog_cancel_ok_buttons` editor setting and by default it's platform-dependent. The screenshot was taken on Linux with KDE.

> The "confirm" button saying "I understand the risk" maybe could say something like "I understand the risk, continue" so that it's more explicitly performing the operation?

Yeah I thought about that, but I didn't want the button to be too long. I think the dialog could also better explain the shortcomings of renaming, because some of them are known (e.g. the exported variables), but again, listing everything would make the text super long xd If anyone has better idea, it can be applied in a follow-up PR.
